dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is scheduling and calendar management, and the disclosed tools match that purpose: listing calendars and events, checking availability, resolving contacts, composing proposals, and creating bookings. Creating bookings is high-impact but expected for this skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions include clear user-control safeguards: discover calendars first, check availability before booking, confirm booking details before book_slot or request_booking, confirm ambiguous contact matches, and never auto-send proposals.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a pinned external npm MCP package, @temporal-cortex/cortex-mcp@0.9.1, which downloads a platform binary and claims checksum verification. This is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but users are still trusting the external package and release pipeline.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: OAuth calendar credentials and network access to Google, Microsoft Graph, CalDAV, and optional api.temporal-cortex.com are proportionate to the scheduling purpose and are described with Local Mode versus Platform Mode boundaries.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Persistent state is disclosed as OAuth credentials and config under ~/.config/temporal-cortex/. I found no artifact-backed hidden persistence, privilege escalation, destructive deletion, or unrelated local data access.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: calendar-scheduling
Version: 0.9.1

The calendar-scheduling skill is a well-documented tool for managing Google, Outlook, and CalDAV calendars via a Rust-based MCP server (@temporal-cortex/cortex-mcp). It demonstrates strong security practices, including local-only credential storage in ~/.config/temporal-cortex/, automated SHA256 checksum verification during installation, and a built-in 'prompt injection firewall' for event content. The instructions in SKILL.md are focused on safety workflows, such as requiring user confirmation before booking or sending proposals, and the network scope is transparently limited to calendar providers and an optional platform API (api.temporal-cortex.com) for cross-user scheduling.
